label: Copy-phase recall, strongest when outputting l/h/d/b/i/x/q/v/m/3/0/n
explanation: Broad copy-phase feature. 99.8% of activation mass falls in the copy phase (t > L, recall_idx >= 1). It is almost silent in the original phase and on the <DEL> step, and fires on about 53% of copy steps. Within the copy phase, firing rate and magnitude depend on the identity of the token being output: out_tok l/h/d/b fires about 80% of the time (lift 3.5x), and l and h carry the most mass. The top activations come when the model outputs l (or h) during runs like ...h l l l..., and activation stays elevated over the neighbouring outputs. Upcoming outputs (next_out l/h) add a little. It does not depend on L, digit count or first token. phase==2 alone gives recall 0.995 at precision 0.53 (F1 0.69). Restricting to a 12-token out_tok set gives precision 0.83, recall 0.62 and mass recall 0.77 (dev F1 0.71). Firing on the other output tokens is weaker and less consistent.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: h, l, d, b, i, x; least: e, z, j, t) and the next token to output (most: l, h, d, x, i, m; least: c, z, j, t); timing cues that raise it most: phase=2, t=3, recall_idx=2.
